g.text: A patron places a hold in the catalogue app. The
service keeps a line of holds for each title, sets a
returned copy aside at the patron's branch, and
tells the patron it is ready to collect.
Branch staff track holds on paper slips and by phone.
A patron must call or visit a branch to place a hold.
Staff phone each patron when a held copy comes in.
A lost slip takes the patron's place in line with it.

WHEN A PICK FAILS OR A HOLD GOES UNCLAIMED
a failed pick never blocks the queue
A failed copy lookup or notifier call retries the hold job with backoff, three attempts in all.
After the third failure the job moves to a dead-letter subscription and the desk lists the hold as stuck.
An unclaimed copy sends a reminder on day five; the patron can extend the hold once or cancel it.
A branch with more than ten stuck holds in an hour pages the service owner.

what the service asks of its patrons
Each flag on the drawings marks where its note applies.
A hold reaches the pick queue only once its patron has confirmed the branch.
The worker never sets a copy aside for an unconfirmed hold.
A hold stores a reference to the copy record, never a copy of it.
The notifier holds no credentials for the holds store.
The blocked line in view 3 is a database grant, not a convention.
Out of scope: interlibrary loans, fines, and holds on e-books.
